Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time officially shut down, co-founder Antonio Pinto immediately announced the launch of a brand-new TV and film tracking app called Bingers, which will place greater emphasis on social features. Here are the details.

Bingers is now available for download

When Whip Media announced the closure of TV Time, one of the co-founders promptly announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as "a fast and beautiful wish list paired with a fun and engaging community."

According to an exclusive report by TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android platforms, offering a kind of spiritual continuation for users who have long been searching for a replacement — after all, TV Time was once one of the most popular TV tracking apps in the world.

Former users who saved their data through TV Time's export tool before it shut down can import their archives into Bingers and enjoy a seamless transition; as for users who never exported their data, or new users who are using a TV tracking app for the first time, they can start from scratch to build their own viewing records.

Bingers has significantly enhanced its community-driven features, including user profiles, comments, show ratings, GIF animations, polls, and character popularity battles, among others. Pinto told TechCrunch that these are precisely the key elements that made TV Time beloved by users over the years:

For users who simply want to record the TV shows and movies they have watched, Bingers offers standalone wish list and viewing record features. Similar to TV Time, the app also displays an upcoming and premiere schedule calendar, with a countdown feature indicating how many days are left until each show's premiere.

Bingers is now available for free download on the App Store, and currently there are no in-app purchases.
